findings.title: End-of-life operating system
findings.detail: These devices run an OS or firmware past vendor end of support and no longer receive security patches.
findings.remediation: Plan upgrade or replacement; isolate on a restricted VLAN in the meantime.

findings.title: SNMP responds to a default community string
findings.detail: The device answers SNMP with 'public' or 'private'. Anyone on the LAN can read its configuration details; 'private' may allow writes.
findings.remediation: Change community strings to long random values, restrict SNMP by ACL to the monitoring host, or move to SNMPv3 authPriv.

findings.title: Telnet enabled
findings.detail: Telnet sends credentials and sessions in cleartext. Anyone on the network path can capture admin passwords.
findings.remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH. On Cisco: `line vty 0 15` → `transport input ssh`.

findings.title: Windows updates not installed in 60+ days
findings.detail: These hosts' most recent update is more than two months old, so recent security fixes are missing.
findings.remediation: Check the RMM patch policy / WSUS approvals and remediate failing installs.

findings.title: Automatic logon configured
findings.detail: Windows is set to log on automatically, which usually means a password is stored in the registry.
findings.remediation: Remove AutoAdminLogon and DefaultPassword from the Winlogon registry key.

findings.title: Enable password stored with weak encryption
findings.detail: The switch uses `enable password` (reversible) instead of `enable secret`.
findings.remediation: Replace with `enable algorithm-type scrypt secret …` and remove `enable password`.

findings.title: Real-time antivirus protection is off
findings.detail: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is disabled and no other antivirus product is registered.
findings.remediation: Re-enable Defender real-time protection or deploy the MSP's EDR agent.

findings.title: SMBv1 enabled
findings.detail: SMBv1 is the protocol abused by WannaCry/NotPetya (EternalBlue) and is deprecated by Microsoft.
findings.remediation: Disable SMB1: `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol`; on NAS devices set minimum protocol to SMB2.

findings.title: Telnet allowed on management lines (VTY)
findings.detail: The config permits Telnet logins to the device.
findings.remediation: Set `transport input ssh` on all `line vty` blocks.

findings.title: Multiple DHCP servers on one segment
findings.detail: More than one DHCP server answered: 10.20.0.10, 192.168.0.1. A rogue DHCP server can redirect clients' gateway/DNS (man-in-the-middle) or cause outages.
findings.remediation: Identify the unauthorized server; enable DHCP snooping on access switches.

findings.title: Management web UI over plain HTTP
findings.detail: Infrastructure devices offer their admin page without HTTPS, exposing admin credentials on the wire.
findings.remediation: Enable HTTPS-only management and disable the HTTP listener.

findings.title: SMB signing not required on servers
findings.detail: Without required signing, SMB relay attacks (e.g. NTLM relay) can impersonate users against these servers.
findings.remediation: Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' via GPO.

findings.title: System drive not encrypted (BitLocker off)
findings.detail: Workstations' C: drive is unencrypted; a lost or stolen device exposes its data.
findings.remediation: Enable BitLocker with TPM and escrow recovery keys to Entra ID / AD.

findings.title: Expired TLS certificates
findings.detail: Services are presenting certificates that have already expired; users learn to click through warnings.
findings.remediation: Renew the certificates (or automate with ACME/internal CA).

findings.title: FTP service exposed
findings.detail: FTP transfers credentials and files unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Replace with SFTP/FTPS, or disable the service if it is not needed.

findings.title: Local accounts with weak password storage
findings.detail: `username … password 0/7` stores passwords in clear text or a trivially reversible form.
findings.remediation: Use `username … secret` (type 8/9).

findings.title: Switch/router interfaces with errors
findings.detail: Interfaces report a high error count (CRC/frame errors), commonly a bad cable, duplex mismatch or failing optic.
findings.remediation: Check cabling and duplex settings on the listed devices' ports.

findings.title: Too many local administrators
findings.detail: Some hosts have more than four members in the local Administrators group (up to 6).
findings.remediation: Limit local admin to a managed group (e.g. LAPS + a tier-1 admin group).

findings.title: UPnP enabled on the gateway
findings.detail: UPnP lets any internal device open inbound ports on the firewall without admin approval.
findings.remediation: Disable UPnP/NAT-PMP on the edge device.

findings.title: Unencrypted HTTP management enabled in config
findings.detail: `ip http server` is enabled.
findings.remediation: Use `no ip http server` and `ip http secure-server` only if the web UI is needed.

findings.title: RDP enabled on workstations
findings.detail: Remote Desktop listening on endpoints widens the lateral-movement surface for ransomware.
findings.remediation: Disable RDP on workstations or restrict it by firewall to admin jump hosts; require NLA.

findings.title: SNMP v1/v2c in use
findings.detail: Community strings travel in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Migrate monitoring to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy (SHA/AES).

findings.title: AAA not enabled
findings.detail: `aaa new-model` is off, so logins can't be centralised or audited.
findings.remediation: Enable AAA with RADIUS/TACACS+ and local fallback.

findings.title: Infrastructure not rebooted in over a year
findings.detail: Uptime over a year usually means firmware has not been patched.
findings.remediation: Schedule firmware updates in a maintenance window.

findings.title: No NTP server configured
findings.detail: Without NTP, log timestamps drift and certificate checks can fail.
findings.remediation: Point the device at internal or public NTP servers.

findings.title: No remote syslog configured
findings.detail: Device logs stay local and are lost on reboot, so incidents can't be investigated.
findings.remediation: Send logs to the MSP's syslog/SIEM collector.

findings.title: Reboot pending to finish updates
findings.detail: Installed updates won't take effect until these hosts restart.
findings.remediation: Schedule a restart.

findings.title: TLS certificates expiring within 30 days
findings.detail: Certificates will expire soon and cause outages or browser warnings.
findings.remediation: Renew before expiry.

findings.title: Self-signed certificates on management interfaces
findings.detail: Self-signed certificates can't be distinguished from an attacker's certificate by users.
findings.remediation: Issue certificates from an internal CA and distribute the root via GPO/MDM.

findings.title: Unidentified devices
findings.detail: These devices answered on the network but OctoLAN could not determine what they are (no hostname, open services, SNMP or vendor match).
findings.remediation: Identify and label each device. Unknown devices are a common source of shadow IT and unmanaged risk.

findings.title: Saved credentials were rejected
findings.detail: The customer-provided credentials didn't work on these hosts, so they were assessed without logging in.
findings.remediation: Confirm the account with the customer (expired password, missing admin rights, or a different domain).
